concerns.text: T001 requires executing `python -m code.pipeline.run_all` with exit 0 and a pytest run of `code/tests/` captured in pipeline.log ending `STATUS: SUCCESS` — but run_all orchestrates 'the full sequence' whose components (scoring T002, simulation T003, compliance T004, merge T005, analysis T006) do not exist yet at T001. This is a consumer-before-producer ordering violation: T001's own verification cannot pass until T006+ are done. Either scope T001's verification to a skeleton smoke (e.g., run_all --check or a stub stage list) or move the full-run verification to T010.

T003 (Phase 1) must produce `smoke_results.json` 'with one entry per metric … all values computed from the actual bootstrap output' — but the bootstrap analysis is implemented in T006 (Phase 2). T003 consumes an artifact whose producer comes later. Reorder (bootstrap smoke before T003's verification) or restate T003's smoke values as coming from a minimal inline bootstrap defined within T003.

T003 is tagged [P] (parallel-safe) but it depends on T001's directory structure/config and on T002's scoring functions (it emits 'scored records' via simulate_study.py), and it writes into `data/raw/` and `data/results/` that T001 creates. Hidden ordering requirement + shared filesystem state — the [P] tag is unsafe; remove it or make T003 self-contained.

T010 is tagged [P] but compiles the final report from T006's statistical_summary.json, T008's sensitivity outputs, T009's figures, and re-runs the quickstart end-to-end (T010's test_end_to_end re-executes the whole pipeline). It has explicit ordering dependencies on nearly every prior task — not parallel-safe.

T003's simulate_study.py emits 'scored records' implying it uses T002's scoring functions, but the dependency is only implicit. The stated execution order (T002 → T003) is correct; make the dependency explicit in T003's description or the dependency table to prevent reordering.
